artifacts.notes: Optical character recognition of a densely set nineteenth-century Bible in two type sizes. The notes are printed in a smaller face than the scriptural text and their initialled attributions are frequently corrupted. It is a finding aid; the presence or absence of a note at a given verse is legible from it, but the exact wording of a note is not established by it alone.
artifacts.rights_basis: A nineteenth-century English printing whose compiler died in 1849; out of copyright by age. The Internet Archive text layer is a mechanical derivative of a scan of a public-domain book and carries no separate creative claim asserted by the host.

edition.publication: A nineteenth-century printing whose title page year is not recorded in the digitization consulted
edition.title: The Douay-Rheims Bible with Haydock's commentary, the printing digitized as Internet Archive item haydock-douay-rheims-catholic-bible

work.author: George Leo Haydock, compiler
work.description: Haydock's annotated Douay-Rheims, first issued in parts from 1811 and reprinted through the nineteenth century. The commentary is a compilation of Catholic exegetes with initialled attributions: C. for Calmet, H. for Haydock, M. for Menochius, W. for Worthington, and others, expanded in the edition's own key. The scriptural text it prints is Challoner's revision; the notes are the work registered here. A locus is BookToken.chapter.verse.
work.title: The Douay-Rheims Bible with a Comprehensive Catholic Commentary
